data.name: Shrayan
data.gender_notes: Shrayan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘shruti’ meaning ‘that which is heard’. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is referred to as Shreyas or Shreyaan, the one who bestows knowledge and wisdom. The name Shrayan carries the meaning “Knowledge, Wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shrayan usually hope their child will grow to embody knowledge, wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Shrayan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Knowledge, Wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shrayan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

vedic_reference.note: Shrayan is a name found in various Hindu scriptures and mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit root 'shri', which is associated with the goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and prosperity. The name Shrayan is also associated with the deity Vishnu, who is known as the preserver of the universe.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu calendars mark the month of Shravan as the month of Hari, or Vishnu. It is believed that bathing in rivers during this month bestows special merit.

Another reference states that Shravan is the name of the god of the same name, who is believed to be the presiding deity of the sacred river Saraswati. Mythological texts describe Shravan as an ascetic who undertook severe penance to please Lord Shiva.
